positions.as_written: Say that posteromedial tibial oedema on the scan should prompt the look even where no tear is reported.
Repair where found, at the same sitting as the reconstruction.
Repair carries the usual meniscal repair restrictions and the usual failure rate, neither of which this page quantifies.
- Posteromedial tibial oedema should prompt the look.
Repair technique and whether a stable lesion needs repair at all are the technical questions that follow, and they follow the look rather than preceding it.
Residual anterior laxity in a well placed graft should prompt a question about the posteromedial corner of the meniscus before a question about the graft.
Take all five explicitly rather than by impression, and say before the operation that the look will be done and what it might lead to.
